item.title: 2 Chainz Says He Suffered Broken Bones In Cybertruck Crash
item.dc:creator: Chuck Creekmur (@ChuckCreekmur)
item.description: 2 Chainz says he’s recovering from broken ribs after another driver swerved into his car to avoid a hitting a possum.
item.content:encoded:
2 Chainz says he’s resting with broken ribs after a head-on crash sent his Tesla Cybertruck into a utility pole, and his account of how it started involves a possum.

According to Tity Boi, the other driver swerved to avoid the animal and hit him head-on. If you were wondering how the truck ended up against a pole, that’s the rapper’s account. Where the possum ended up is anybody’s guess.

Chainz shared an update after hearing from people concerned about his condition.

“A lot of calls and concern on my well being, i appreciate everyone who reaching out, im good, just resting with broke ribs, no I wasn’t drinking, smoking ,sleeping or on auto pilot, the other driver dodged a possum and hit me head on, smh, hope that answers all of your questions, Blessed.”

He managed to thank everybody and get ahead of four different theories in one breath. That last word, though, is the one I kept coming back to after watching what he posted from the scene.

The video shows Chainz getting away from the wreckage and lying in the grass. The truck’s airbags had gone off, and the windshield and windows were smashed. You can hear him groaning as he takes in the damage. The man loved that truck. I can see why he needed a minute to look at it, even with everything else going on.

There were no other reported injuries. That’s a relief when you consider how much damage is visible in the clip and how easily a swerve to miss an animal, as Chainz describes it, can turn into something much worse.

I’m glad he was able to give everybody an update himself. The Cybertruck can wait. As for the folks who already had a theory about what he was doing behind the wheel, Chainz just gave them four separate reasons to put the phone down.

item.title: Quavo-Backed V12 Restaurant Closes In Atlanta After Two Years
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Quavo and the Watson siblings opened V12 above a Midtown gas station in 2024. The Atlanta restaurant has now closed for good.
item.content:encoded:
Quavo‘s venture in a Midtown Atlanta sports bar has come to an end. V12 Restaurant & Sports Bar, which the Migos rapper opened with Vinny and Kelan Watson and their sister, Simone Hopson, has closed permanently after about two and a half years.

The owners announced the immediate shutdown in an Instagram statement.

They said they made the decision “after much thought and consideration” and credited Quavo’s partnership with bringing “music, culture, hospitality, and Atlanta’s energy under one roof.”

Watson thanked his sisters, staff and guests in the same statement. The owners gave no reason for the closure and didn’t say what they’d do next with the V12 Restaurant Group.

The restaurant opened to the public on May 4, 2024, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported.

It took up space above a BP gas station on Spring Street, across from The Varsity. The unusual address fed into the name: V12 refers to the engine found in some high-end cars.

Quavo was already a regular at the Watsons’ Buckhead dessert shop and cocktail bar, Sovereign Sweets, when he asked about going into business with them. The siblings were already working on V12 when Vinny brought him into the project, according to The Atlanta Journal-Constitution.

T.I. and 2 Chainz turned up for the ribbon cutting.

Fulton County Commissioner Natalie Hall and South Fulton Councilwoman Carmalitha L. Gumbs presented a proclamation to Quavo, Vinny and Kelan at the opening.

A replica Lamborghini built for Quavo’s “Lamb Talk” performance on The Tonight Show hung from the ceiling. More than 20 TVs carried sports, and an Axios Atlanta visit described private rooms and a terrace overlooking Midtown. The room could seat up to 250 people.

Hopson ran the drinks program, using cars with V12 engines as namesakes for seven cocktails. The Maybach Sour, for example, paired whisky with a red wine float.

“We wanted to create a menu that was comfort food with classic and contemporary cuisine, but elevated,” Vinny told the AJC.

The Watsons came to the project with years in hospitality, while the AJC described V12 as Quavo’s first business in that field. Soon after opening, AllHipHop covered Lana Del Rey’s visit to V12 after she was filmed dancing there.

item.title: Macklemore Says Free Palestine Tour Raised More Than $2.25 Million
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Macklemore reported that ticket sales, merchandise, donations and partners raised more than $2.25 million for Palestinian causes.
item.content:encoded:
Macklemore says his Free Palestine Tour raised more than $2.25 million for groups that support Palestinians.

He shared the figures on Instagram after playing three benefit shows in Europe.

The partner groups raised more than half the money through their own networks, according to figures from the tour’s impact report.

The report counted 3,884 contributors and also factored in merchandise sales, ticket revenue after production costs and money given directly to the tour.

The report says the tour split direct donations evenly among 12 groups, including Gaza Soup Kitchen, Medical Aid for Palestinians, the Palestine Children’s Relief Fund and HEAL Palestine.

Other recipients included Anera, GLIA Equal Care, Jewish Voice for Peace, the Institute for Middle East Understanding, the Middle East Children’s Alliance, the Palestinian Youth Movement, Taawon for Palestine and UNRWA.

One of the recipients, HEAL Palestine, brought families from Gaza to the shows.

In the tour report, co-founder Dr. Zeena Salman recalled meeting a mother whose young son had lost a leg. What stayed with Salman was the mother’s gratitude at finding herself among 15,000 people who cared about Palestinians.

“We’re asking everyone in those rooms, and everyone following along, to turn that solidarity into HEALing for Gaza’s children,” HEAL Palestine said during the tour.

The group’s work with children who have lost limbs starts with medical care and includes physical therapy before a child can be fitted with a prosthesis.

For children who need treatment they can’t get in Gaza, HEAL arranges for family members to travel with them and for schooling to continue while they’re away. Children in the program have received care in Egypt, Spain and the United States.

In Gaza, the group also runs a soccer academy for amputees and a swimming program called Waves of Hope.

The Gaza Children’s Choir took part in the opening concert on October 26 at Dublin’s 3Arena, appearing on video. Macklemore shared the Dublin bill with Dead Prez and Kneecap as well as Palestinian singer Lina Makoul before playing Paris on October 29 and London’s OVO Arena Wembley on October 30.

The report directs listeners who still want to contribute to the Macklemore Fund for Palestine through the nonprofit PLUS1.

item.title: Steve Lacy Books London Arena Headline Show At The O2
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Steve Lacy brings his new album to London's O2 next April, with a presale before tickets go on sale to the public.
item.content:encoded:
Steve Lacy is taking the tour for his first album in four years to one of London’s biggest stages.

The singer and guitarist will headline The O2 on April 26, 2027, behind his third solo album, Oh yeah?.

London is the first stop on the spring European leg, with dates to follow in Amsterdam and Paris before the run ends in Prague.

Tickets for the London show go on sale at 10 a.m. local time Friday, November 27, according to The O2. Live Nation is offering early access through its My Live Nation registration.

The European dates extend an Oh yeah? tour that brought Lacy back to the West Coast this week.

Lacy sold out the Hollywood Bowl on November 21, his biggest headline show to date, and brought out guests including SZA and Tyler, The Creator.

He then headed to San Francisco for two nights at the Bill Graham Civic Auditorium. The San Francisco shows are scheduled for November 24 and 25.

Before the Hollywood Bowl date, Lacy gave Los Angeles a preview of how the new songs sit with his older material.

He played “nothing” and “the feeling” alongside “Dark Red” and “C U Girl” at Tyler, The Creator’s Camp Flog Gnaw festival.

The album that connects those dates came out July 17 through RCA Records. Lead single “the feeling” is one of 10 tracks, and Lacy splits the guest spots among three singers: Erykah Badu on “pure colour,” Cecile Believe on “lovesexdrugbomb” and SZA on “is it cool?”

Lacy worked on the album in Paris but told Apple Music’s Zane Lowe in an interview that he measures its reception onstage. “But I don’t really know what’s real yet until I go out and play it and see it and sing it together with people,” Lacy said.

That last album, 2022’s Gemini Rights, gave Lacy his first No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 with “Bad Habit.” The Recording Academy named Gemini Rights best progressive R&B album in 2023, and Lacy performed the single at the ceremony. The song was nominated for record of the year, song of the year and best pop solo performance.

The O2’s listing has doors opening at 6:30 p.m. local time on the night of the concert.

item.title: Stevie Wonder Teases New Music As Howard University Celebrates 50 Years of “Songs In The Key of Life”
item.dc:creator: Chuck Creekmur (@ChuckCreekmur)
item.description: Stevie Wonder revealed “Fear Can’t Put Dreams to Sleep” from his next project as Howard University celebrated 50 years of Songs in the Key of Life.
item.content:encoded:
Iconic artist Stevie Wonder shared a new detail about his long-discussed project Through the Eyes of Wonder on Tuesday (Nov. 24), telling a Howard University audience it includes a song called “Fear Can’t Put Dreams to Sleep.”

He also named another future song, “Truth Is a Light,” during a student-led celebration of the 50th anniversary of Songs in the Key of Life.

Wonder had publicly discussed Through the Eyes of Wonder as early as 2020.

At Howard, he gave no release date and did not say whether “Truth Is a Light” would also appear on the project. He told the audience his voice was too rough to sing “Fear Can’t Put Dreams to Sleep” that day, but he delivered its message in his own words. 

“You must never ever let any leader, any group of people, anyone ever allow fear to put your dreams to sleep.”

The campus visit came a day after Wonder’s 50th-anniversary tour stop at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C. At Howard’s Cramton Auditorium, students and university ensembles paid tribute with A Love Letter to Stevie Wonder: Celebrating 50 Years of Songs in the Key of Life. The program billed the marching band for “Another Star,” the gospel choir for “Sir Duke” and “As,” and Gavin Christian for a cello performance of “If It’s Magic.”

Jasmine “Jazz” Young, director of Howard’s Warner Music/Blavatnik Center for Music & Entertainment Business, told Wonder and his family she was fighting tears as she welcomed them.

Young, who got her start in the music industry at Howard, spoke about the lives Wonder had touched and the doors he had opened. 

“You are a voice for the voiceless, a champion for justice, and a true living example of what happens when extraordinary talent meets extraordinary purpose,” Young said. “Today, as we celebrate 50 years of your masterpiece Songs in the Key of Life, we also celebrate the lives that you have touched and the doors that you have opened.”

Wonder established a scholarship for Howard students pursuing music, and the university presented him with its Presidential Medal in recognition of his legacy in music and the humanities.

One of his children, Mandla Morris, who had watched friends and peers perform, offered a more personal tribute. “You guys see Stevie Wonder, but I see Steve Morris,” they told the audience. Morris is a creative that is in fashion design, music, and acting.

“Wow, this looks good on me,” Wonder said after accepting the medal from Dr. Wayne A. I. Frederick, Howard’s interim president.

Finally, with his youngest daughter’s birthday three days away, he asked the room to sing his version of “Happy Birthday” to her.

item.title: Mary J. Blige’s “Real Love” Beats Copyright Challenge On Appeal
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Mary J. Blige's breakout hit stays clear of a copyright claim as a judge's dismissal stands in the fight over its drums.
item.content:encoded:
Mary J. Blige scored one of her first hits with “Real Love,” and a federal appeals court has now turned away a copyright challenge to the song.

The Second Circuit upheld the dismissal on Monday, November 23, leaving the publisher, Songs of Universal, with a win over Tuff City Records.

The dispute traced a drum passage through three records.

Tuff City said the Honey Drippers’ 1973 protest song “Impeach the President” supplied the drum sounds for Audio Two’s “Top Billin’,” which was then sampled on Blige’s 1992 single.

Tuff City owns copyrights in both the Honey Drippers’ recording and the composition, but the claim the panel reviewed concerned the composition.

That meant the court had to consider how much of the earlier song’s protected musical writing carried over into “Real Love,” not simply whether a bit of the recording traveled from one track to another.

The judges found differences in everything from the lyrics to the way the tracks were arranged.

“Impeach the President” has a group vocal with call-and-response, horns and guitars, while Blige sings over piano and percussion.

“The songs differ in their lyrics, melody, genre, subject matter, and overall sound,” the judges wrote in their summary order.

Songs of Universal did not dispute that copying occurred.

The panel said the “Real Love” composition was “not substantially similar to that work,” even if the percussion Tuff City pointed to qualified for protection.

The judges also left in place orders keeping parts of a settlement between Tuff City and a separate Universal affiliate out of the public record.

Tuff City brought the case in April 2024 and asked for damages and an order blocking use of the disputed material, as AllHipHop previously reported.

U.S. District Judge Dale Ho tossed the case in September 2025 and did not give Tuff City another chance to rewrite its complaint.

The appeals court left that decision in place along with the ruling on the copyright claim.

“Real Love” was a single from Blige’s debut album, What’s the 411?, and climbed to No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100. Tuff City sued over the song but did not name Blige as a defendant.

Tuff City attorney Hillel Parness told Billboard that his client plans to challenge the ruling.

item.title: “Michael” Director Antoine Fuqua Sued Over Alleged Gun Attack Outside Hollywood Bar
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: A Hollywood bar manager alleges "Michael" director Antoine Fuqua hit him with a handgun after a dispute outside the venue.
item.content:encoded:
Antoine Fuqua, who directed the Michael Jackson biopic Michael, is being sued by a Hollywood bar employee who says the filmmaker hit him in the face with a handgun.

William Rosenthal, an assistant manager at Good Times at Davey Wayne’s, says the encounter left him with a broken nose and a head injury.

“What’s claimed in that filing about Antoine is not true,” Fuqua’s publicist Alan Nierob told Deadline.

Rosenthal filed the 10-page complaint in Los Angeles Superior Court on November 20, accusing Fuqua and Fuqua’s son, Brando, of assault, battery and intentionally causing emotional distress.

He wants a jury trial and seeks more than $50,000 in damages, including medical expenses, lost earnings and other relief.

The complaint traces the dispute to a night in February when Rosenthal turned away a group he thought was too intoxicated to enter. Fuqua’s daughter was among them, and Rosenthal told the group to leave after someone spat on him.

Later that night, Fuqua allegedly approached Rosenthal near the bar’s entrance and accused him of pepper-spraying his daughter. When Rosenthal denied it, the director allegedly hit him with a handgun, used a racial and antisemitic slur and threatened to kill him.

The complaint alleges Brando swung a second handgun at Rosenthal as he staggered, then both men pointed their weapons at him before leaving.

Rosenthal attributes cuts, lasting scars and post-traumatic stress disorder to the encounter and says his injuries could leave him permanently disabled.

Fuqua directed Jaafar Jackson as his uncle in Michael. The film crossed $1 billion worldwide in July.

The biopic follows Jackson from his years in the Jackson Five into his solo career, with Colman Domingo and Nia Long playing his parents. Fuqua’s earlier films include Training Day and The Equalizer.

Lionsgate has confirmed that a sequel is in development.

item.title: Lizzo Flies To Minneapolis As Longtime DJ Sophia Eris Recovers From Brain Surgery
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lizzo flew to Minneapolis to support longtime DJ Sophia Eris after emergency surgery, as friends plan a benefit.
item.content:encoded:
Lizzo flew to Minneapolis to help Sophia Eris after her longtime DJ and former rap group bandmate underwent emergency brain surgery.

Friends of the Minneapolis artist launched a recovery fund and are planning a benefit with local performers.

Eris, whose name is Lauren Alford, was on her way home Thursday night when she suffered a brain aneurysm, according to the fundraiser.

“Thankfully, Lauren made it through surgery and is now recovering,” organizer Mica Grimm wrote. Grimm said the recovery was uncertain and would require ongoing care. Eris’ parents traveled from Florida to be with her.

Lizzo said Eris was more like a sister than a friend.

“I am in direct communication with her family, I flew to Minneapolis, and am helping in every single way I can,” Lizzo wrote on Instagram.

The fundraiser is raising money on behalf of Eris’ family to cover medical bills, recovery needs and unexpected expenses. It showed more than $15,000 toward a $30,000 goal Monday, November 23.

Grimm said friends and fellow musicians were working on the benefit and would share more details later.

Before she toured with Lizzo, Eris was already making music with her in the Twin Cities. The two worked together in The Chalice and later in GRRRL PRTY, the Minneapolis collective that played its final show at Rock the Garden in 2016.

In an interview with Slam Academy, Eris talked about learning to DJ on the job after Lizzo asked her to come along on her first tour. By the time of that conversation, Eris had returned from a year of arena shows with the singer.

Eris built a career in Minneapolis outside that tour, too. She hosted mornings at Hip-Hop station Go 95.3 and formed the duo Makr & Eris. First Avenue’s artist bio also credits her on “BOYTROUBLE,” a track by Prince’s band 3RDEYEGIRL.

AllHipHop previously reported how close Lizzo came to walking away from rap before she broke through.

Eris was part of the Minneapolis chapter that came before those hits, when they were recording and performing together rather than working as an arena act.

Friends have not yet announced a date or venue for the benefit.

item.title: iLoveMakonnen Finds Purpose Stocking Shelves At Portland Supermarket Job
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: iLoveMakonnen finds purpose on the supermarket floor in Portland while a new record with Key! brings him back to the studio.
item.content:encoded:
iLoveMakonnen works at a Portland supermarket where his job is to keep the shelves stocked. In an interview with Variety, the “Tuesday” artist spoke about what he gets out of the work. “I’m feeling useful as a human again,” he said, adding, “I’m not useful in music anymore.”

The last time people saw iLoveMakonnen working a shift in Portland, some mistook his appearance behind a restaurant counter for a sign he had fallen on hard times. In August 2025, he flipped burgers at Little Griddle to help a local recording studio called Burn Money Studios recover from a fire. One TikTok from the restaurant drew more than 1.3 million views. He told Variety the attention brought in customers but eventually got in the way of running the place.

His life outside those shifts looks different from the one he led after Drake remixed “Tuesday” in 2014. The two earned a Grammy nomination for best rap/sung collaboration, and iLoveMakonnen signed to Drake’s OVO Sound. When he weighed leaving New York, an Oregon emblem on a toy his dogs were chewing caught his eye. He looked into what housing cost there and realized he could afford to move.

In Portland, he spends time walking through Laurelhurst Park or Unthank Park. Getting people out to see him play in his adopted city has been harder. He told Variety that even with his name on the bill as a co-headliner at Pride in Demand: Portland Queer Takeover, he played to one of the smallest crowds of his career. He also told the magazine he believes coming out as gay has made it harder for him to get booked.

The experience of getting booked for shows hasn’t kept him from recording with longtime collaborator Key!, who joined him on “Lie 2 Me,” a single they released November 13. The two have a joint album called Over It on the way, and iLoveMakonnen told Variety he enjoys the work they do together. “It feels like therapy. It doesn’t feel like a job,” iLoveMakonnen said.

Portland may not be home much longer: iLoveMakonnen told Variety he wants to move to Atlanta.

item.title: Usher And Chris Brown Tour Performer Needed No Emergency Aid After Fall
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: New Orleans fire officials give an update on the performer who fell during Usher and Chris Brown's Superdome stop.
item.content:encoded:
The fire performer who fell offstage at Usher and Chris Brown’s New Orleans concert didn’t need emergency help, according to the New Orleans Fire Department.

A spokesperson for the department told the Los Angeles Times on Tuesday that the fall happened during the tour’s two-night stop at the Caesars Superdome.

The department had “a Pyrotechnic detail working each night of this concert,” the spokesperson said. “The pyro performer was uninjured and did not require emergency assistance following his fall,” the spokesperson told the Times.

The fall came during a routine with two lit batons on the second night of the New Orleans stop.

In the footage from the concert, flames appear to catch on the performer’s costume as he backs toward the stairs. He drops out of view at the bottom of the steps and then returns to the stage; someone appears on a stretcher later in the clip, but that person hasn’t been identified as the fire performer.

The Saturday show had been added after the tour originally booked one night at the Superdome.

On the first night, a nationwide Ticketmaster outage delayed entry and left people waiting in long lines outside the stadium. Ahead of the second show, Ticketmaster gave concertgoers advice on accessing their tickets after the previous night’s problems.

New Orleans was one of several cities where the production set up for more than one stadium date.

The R&B Tour’s schedule also changed in the closing stretch, with a November 16 date at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood and a December 6 show at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens canceled. October stops in Baltimore, Cincinnati, Indianapolis and Columbia, South Carolina, had already been called off.

The cancellations in October were meant to protect the touring party and crew’s health, the promoter said in a notice to ticket holders.

Ticket holders in Indianapolis were told the money would go back to the original payment method, with refunds on transferred tickets going to the original buyer.

Usher and Chris Brown are scheduled to close the tour on December 12 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida.
